title: Outbound inference request
description: The shape of a chat-completions request Tinman sends to the configured provider. Tinman speaks the OpenAI-compatible protocol, so any compatible endpoint serves. The endpoint, model and credential are resolved from the environment or a dotenv file before the request is built. The endpoint and the credential are transport rather than payload, so they sit beside the body instead of inside it: an earlier revision listed them as body fields, and a second encoder that sent neither could diverge from this contract while the attestation stayed green. Referenced by features/inference-provider.feature.

url.description: The absolute chat-completions endpoint the request addresses, built from the resolved base URL.

authorization.description: The Authorization header value. The resolved credential is always sent as a bearer token.

body.description: The JSON document sent as the request body, which is the whole of what the provider receives. Nothing outside this object reaches the payload.

model.description: The resolved model identifier the provider is asked to serve.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature from the request's profile. The acronym profile optimizes for novelty and the assistant profile for correctness, so the value is per-profile rather than global.

messages.description: The chat messages, in order. At least one is always present.

reasoning.description: The provider's reasoning control, omitted where a request does not set one. A reasoning model spends its budget on whatever it is asked, and the tagline asks for six words: measured against the configured provider, the request answered nothing inside forty seconds with reasoning left on and one to two seconds with it disabled. This is OpenRouter's parameter rather than a cross-vendor standard, which is the one place the vendor-neutral claim strains; an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that does not know it ignores it.
